Ten years out, kitchen robotics and automated prep equipment will be more capable and more visible in commercial settings, and it is reasonable to expect some routine prep tasks to shift toward automation in industry. The wide uncertainty band applies to how much of commercial kitchen labor automates by 2036, not to whether a beginner needs embodied practice to acquire foundational technique. Embodiment keeps the rating Low even as adjacent industry tasks become more exposed, and the absence of any institutional mandate is irrelevant here because the protective factor is intrinsic to the skill itself.

A decade out, more of the theoretical food-safety and sustainability content could plausibly be delivered through AI tutoring, and the balance of instructional time might shift further toward supervised kitchen practice, particularly as capability-trend research points to faster, more reliable AI explanation of technical safety material. Even so, the central applied task—developing embodied cooking technique safely enough to earn a food-handler credential—remains something a student must do themselves, and the certification exam remains an individually held credential rather than an AI-transferable one. The uncertainty is genuinely wider at ten years for how introductory culinary instruction is structured, but not for whether hands-on skill-building persists as the instrumental core. RST 3875.d: This course concentrates on aspects of cooking with products found in urban agriculture and urban homesteading environments. This includes cooking with local farm and ranch products.
